editorial:
Imagine being the kid everyone picks on, just to find out that the whole world wants to watch you suffer for views. You get introduced to a lonely, overweight teenager that people call Butter. He is tired of being the joke of the town, so he decides to do something wild. He starts a live stream where he plans to eat himself to death in front of everyone on the internet. It is a dark and heavy setup that makes you feel bad for him while also making you wonder why people are so mean online. The vibe is pretty grim, but it keeps you curious about how far he will actually go.

What really works here is how the movie shows the scary side of social media fame. The acting feels real, and the way the tension builds up as more people tune in is pretty intense. While the story is a bit slow in the middle, the ending hits hard. If you like stories about the dark side of the web, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Butter reaching his breaking point as his online audience grows. Instead of a happy ending, he follows through with his dark plan. He pushes his body past the limit while thousands of people watch and cheer him on. It shows that the people watching didn't actually care about him; they just wanted a show. He dies live on camera, leaving the viewers to deal with the guilt of watching it happen.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about social media and human nature.
